slides.title: Polling Overview
content: Polling is a technique where client repeatedly requests server for new data
Client actively asks instead of server pushing updates
Used in chat systems to check for new messages

slides.title: Why Polling is Used
content: Server cannot send data without client request
Polling was used to achieve near real-time updates

slides.title: Types of Polling
content: Polling is divided into short polling and long polling
Both use HTTP protocol for communication
They differ in connection handling and efficiency

slides.title: Short Polling
content: Client sends requests at fixed intervals
Server responds immediately with data or empty response
Connection opens and closes for each request

slides.title: Long Polling
content: Client sends request and waits for server response
Server holds connection until new data arrives
Responds immediately when data is available

slides.title: Long Polling Behavior
content: Server delays response until data is available
Connection stays open for longer duration
Timeout ensures connection does not stay forever

slides.title: System Design Considerations
content: Latency depends on polling method used
Short polling has higher delay based on interval

slides.title: Performance Challenges
content: Each request consumes CPU and memory
Bandwidth wasted due to empty responses
Difficult to scale for millions of users

slides.title: Advantages of Polling
content: Stateless and easy to scale horizontally

slides.title: Disadvantages of Polling
content: Poor scalability with large user base
Thread blocking issues in long polling

slides.title: Key Technical Concepts
content: Latency is delay in data transfer

slides.title: Architecture Concepts
content: Stateless servers do not store session data
Blocking I/O waits for operations to complete

slides.title: Polling vs WebSocket
content: Polling does not maintain persistent connection

slides.title: When to Use Polling
content: Useful when real-time is not required

slides.title: Final Summary
content: Polling is a client-driven communication model
Simple but inefficient for large systems
Long polling improves efficiency but still limited
WebSocket is preferred for modern real-time applications
